sections.h2: Which county tax office bills a Round Rock house
sections.html:
Your bill comes from either the Williamson County or the Travis County tax office, depending on where your parcel sits. Round Rock lies in both counties, and the city contracts with both offices to collect its levy.

  • Williamson County Tax Office, 1848 Texas Trail, Georgetown, 512-943-1601.
  • Travis County Tax Office, 2433 Ridgepoint Dr., Austin, 512-854-9473.
  • Williamson Central Appraisal District, 625 F.M. 1460, Georgetown, 512-930-3787.
  • Travis Central Appraisal District, 850 E Anderson Lane, Austin, 512-834-9317.

Each county runs a lookup site where an address shows what every unit on that parcel charges. Confirm the county before you phone, since each office holds its own accounts.

The city adopted 37.2000 cents on each $100 of assessed value for fiscal year 2025-2026. A median home on the 2025 rolls is worth $395,240, with an estimated city tax bill of $1,470.

Think of the city figure as one line of a longer statement. Other taxing units stack their own lines on the same bill, so the city number alone understates your total. Proposed rates are published every year under Tax Code Section 26.04, and delinquency begins February 1.

sections.h2: When a Round Rock tax bill goes late
sections.html:
Statements arrive in October and January 31 is the last clean day. February 1 starts delinquency: six percent penalty and one percent interest go on at once, and the penalty alone is twelve percent by July 1. If a collection lawyer is involved, as much as 20 percent more can follow.

Anyone can split the bill, paying half by November 30 and half by June 30. Seniors and disabled owners can make four installments. The Comptroller's payment page also explains penalty waivers and homestead payment plans of up to 36 months.

sections.h2: Exemptions and caps that lower the bill
sections.html:
The homestead exemption does the most work. School districts tax $140,000 less of the value, and anyone who is 65-plus or disabled gets another $60,000 off. Cities and counties may add a percentage exemption as large as 20 percent, so ask each office what it chose.

  • A homestead's appraised value can climb no more than 10 percent a year starting after the first qualifying January 1.
  • Seniors can freeze the school bill at whatever it was in their first qualifying year.
  • A disabled veteran gets a partial break that scales with the VA rating, and a 100 percent rating earns a total one.
  • File applications with the appraisal district by April 30, using forms on the Comptroller's exemption page.

A buyer who closes after January 1 on a house whose seller never claimed can file immediately.

sections.h2: How to contest your Round Rock appraised value
sections.html:
Get a written protest to the review board by May 15 or, if your notice came late, within thirty days of getting it. Notices for homesteads start near April 1.

A board ruling you dislike has three more routes: district court, arbitration, and (for values above $1,000,000) the State Office of Administrative Hearings. Whatever you choose, send the portion you do not dispute before delinquency to protect the appeal. Ask the district early for your property record card and its comparable sales, and compare them with recent sales on your own street. Keep the notice, the record card and any photos together so you can show them at the hearing, and note the hearing date so a buyer is not surprised by a pending value.

Population rose 18.2% from the April 2020 base to the July 2025 estimate. The city has 48,647 households of 2.61 people on average, with median income of $99,287. Owners paying a mortgage spend a median $2,364 a month, against $925 for owners with none. A citywide median hides street-level gaps, so weigh your house against recent sales in your subdivision.

sections.h2: Flood control and special district charges
sections.html: Water has been both a limit and a hazard here. Flash floods from Tropical Storm Hermine on September 8, 2010 forced evacuations near Lake Creek and flooded 44 homes, mostly in Round Rock West and on Lake Creek Circle. Voters in the Brushy Creek Water Control and Improvement District approved a small property tax in 2002 to maintain flood control dams. That is the kind of district charge worth finding on your own bill, and a buyer near the creek may ask about it.

A rental of fewer than 30 consecutive days is short-term, and it carries 9 percent of monthly net receipts, built from a 7 percent hotel tax and a 2 percent venue tax.

  • Registration is $35 at first and $25 to renew before January 1.
  • Each property registers separately.
  • A return is filed monthly, including empty months, no later than the final day of the next month.
  • Penalties run 5, 10 or 15 percent by lateness, with 10 percent interest from day 61.
  • Airbnb and Vrbo do not remit this tax on your behalf.

Before selling a house that was rented, file every open return and submit the closure form. A buyer's title company may ask for proof that the account is closed, so keep the confirmation with your sale papers.

Before you list, gather a few things. Order a current statement from whichever county bills your parcel, then list every unit on it, special districts included. If anything is owed, ask that county's tax office for a written payoff, and get it before you sign a contract so the closing office has a firm figure. If a protest is pending, keep the filing and the hearing date handy so a buyer knows which value the tax will follow.

A lien for each year's tax forms on January 1 and rides with the house. A buyer cannot get clean title until delinquent balances are cleared, and the January 1 owner remains answerable for that year even after the transfer.

The escrow officer pays the account out of the buyer's money when the sale funds, so a written payoff from the correct county, special district balance included, is worth getting early. The county clerk records the deed, and the state's clerk manual lists $5.00 for page one plus $4.00 per added page. A cash buyer can skip a lender's timeline, but the tax payoff is still cleared at the table.

faqs.q: What per-$100 rate does Round Rock charge?
faqs.a: Round Rock adopted 37.2000 cents per $100 for fiscal year 2025-2026. Each county, school and special district sets its own rate.

faqs.q: Williamson County or Travis County: which gets my payment?
faqs.a: Pay the county that contains your parcel. The city contracts with both offices, and each property falls under only one. A lookup by address settles it.

faqs.q: What if I miss the January 31 date?
faqs.a: It turns delinquent on February 1 and picks up penalty and interest immediately. The penalty grows to twelve percent by July 1 and interest keeps running.

faqs.q: Is hotel tax due on an Airbnb in Round Rock?
faqs.a: Yes. Stays under 30 days owe 9 percent of net receipts, split 7 and 2 between the hotel and venue taxes. You register each property and file monthly.

faqs.q: Can a Round Rock house with back taxes still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance gets paid at closing. Get the payoff in writing from the right county beforehand so you can calculate your net.
